steps.b: At six in the morning, the school kitchen was empty except for Lily and a radio crackling out the weather.
steps.reveal: The second opening answers two questions at once: when (six in the morning) and where (the school kitchen). That's setting, and it puts the reader right there.

cards.title: Setting = when + where
cards.body: The setting is when and where a story happens. When can be a time of day, a season, or even a year long ago or far in the future. Where can be as big as a city or as small as a cupboard.

cards.title: General vs. specific
cards.telling: They were at the beach in summer.
cards.showing: The sand burned their feet, and an ice-cream van played its tinny song by the car park.
cards.note: The second version never says "summer" or "beach", but specific details make you see and feel it.

cards.title: Pick details only this place has
cards.body: Every kitchen has a table. Only YOUR kitchen has the table with a burn mark shaped like a boot. One specific detail does more than five general ones.

cards.title: Find when and where
cards.prompt: Tap the two words that tell you when, and the word that tells you where.
cards.text: Late on Sunday night, the empty station smelled of cold coffee and rain.

prompts: Which detail in your snapshot could only belong to that place?
How did you show the time without just naming it?
